title: Paloma and the Orbit
premise: Paloma Delacroix, a memory-smuggler hauling contraband recollections through contested orbits, intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries — the tongue of the Vessari, a people whose annihilation official records insist never happened. The signal carries an intact memory of the massacre, and Paloma, who once smuggled fragments of it for a client they can no longer remember, becomes the only living proof. Hunted by customs enforcers and the corporate archivists rewriting history, Paloma must choose between selling the memory to buy their own survival and broadcasting it to every colony in the system, knowing the act will erase their forged identity and expose the crime that made them a fugitive. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the truth at the cost of their own records — becoming, like the Vessari, officially nonexistent but undeniably real.
about_author: Juniper Voss is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests for stations she refuses to name. She writes about borders, cargo, and the people history loses between the lines.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Running contraband memories past Meridian Station's customs net, Paloma intercepts a repeating distress signal in a dead language. The emotional beat is restless competence cracking into unease — twelve years of routine interrupted by something impossible.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Paloma decodes enough of the signal to realize it's a memory recording: the Vessari massacre, two centuries erased. Their client list includes one name they don't recognize — themselves. Beat: dread dawning through denial.

chapters.title: The Client I Forgot
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, intercut with fragmented first-person memory files. They discover they once smuggled pieces of this very memory and paid for it with chunks of their own past. Beat: identity as unreliable currency.

chapters.title: Customs Hold
chapters.summary: Inspector Rhee Okafor detains Paloma on a routine pretext, probing about 'anomalous transmissions.' Paloma lies well but notices Okafor already knows too much. Beat: the noose tightening while pretending it's small talk.

chapters.title: What the Archive Won't Say
chapters.summary: Paloma visits a black-market archivist, Mirei, who confirms every official record shows the Vessari colony never existed. Someone paid enormously to unmake them. Beat: cold fury replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. To reach the signal's origin coordinates, they must run the Kestrel Corridor, a route that kills one ship in three. They take the job that could fund it — smuggling for the same corporation erasing the record. Beat: complicity as survival.

chapters.title: Ghost Tongue
chapters.summary: Aboard ship, Paloma teaches themself Vessari from the signal itself, and the language starts unlocking buried memories — including a face they loved and lost. Beat: grief surfacing through grammar.

chapters.title: Kestrel Corridor
chapters.summary: A brutal transit sequence: debris fields, a dying scavenger ship Paloma must decide whether to rescue, customs drones. They save one survivor, a girl named Ash. Beat: mercy as risk.

chapters.title: The Colony That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Paloma and Ash reach the coordinates: a hollowed station, scrubbed clean, its walls still holding faint memory residue. Paloma touches a wall and experiences the massacre's final hour. Beat: witness as wound.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: Okafor corners Paloma off the books: hand over the memory, get amnesty, keep your name. She reveals she lost family in another erased event. Beat: temptation wearing a sympathetic face.

chapters.title: Ash's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The girl reveals her colony was also struck from record; she recognized the signal because her grandmother sang in Vessari. Beat: solidarity between the officially dead.

chapters.title: The Archivist's War
chapters.summary: Mirei is raided; her archive burned. Before vanishing she sends Paloma the distribution keys needed to broadcast system-wide. Beat: allies falling, stakes rising.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Lies
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts their own forged identity: the person they were before was a Vessari descendant who survived by forgetting. Beat: the self as the last crime scene.

chapters.title: Running Out of Orbit
chapters.summary: Corporate hunters board Paloma's ship. A desperate flight, Ash wounded, the memory drive cracked — partial corruption begins eating the testimony. Beat: time collapsing.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Dilemma
chapters.summary: Paloma calculates options: sell to a rival power for protection, or broadcast and lose everything, including legal existence. Okafor quietly slips them the customs override codes. Beat: choosing which self survives.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Captured aboard the corporate flagship, Paloma is offered restoration of their true memories — if they surrender the drive. They see their erased life whole and still refuse. Beat: identity reclaimed by refusal.

chapters.title: Ash Decides
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Believing Paloma broken, Ash takes the drive and heads for the broadcast array alone. Beat: the student outgrowing the protector.

chapters.title: The Array at Halo Nine
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Ash reaches the array under fire; Paloma escapes custody using Okafor's codes and races to back her up. Beat: converging desperation.

chapters.title: Every Ear in the System
chapters.summary: Climax part two: together they broadcast the massacre to every colony, station, and ship. The corrupted sections are filled live by Paloma speaking Vessari from memory. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Paloma's records burn in the fallout; they are legally nobody. Okafor resigns rather than file the arrest report. Beat: freedom that feels like amputation.

chapters.title: The Living Record
chapters.summary: Colonies begin honoring the Vessari openly; survivors' descendants surface, including kin of the face from Paloma's buried past. Ash chooses to stay with them. Beat: mourning turning into continuity.

chapters.title: Paloma, Unregistered
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Paloma's POV. Unnamed and untracked, Paloma ships out on a new route, carrying the Vessari language in their head where the contraband used to be. Beat: quiet, earned peace — identity held in memory, not paperwork.
